title: Kernel ideal modules commute with open restriction
statement: Let $i:Z\to Z^\prime$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $V\subseteq Z$ and $V^\prime\subseteq Z^\prime$ be open subschemes with inclusions $j_V,j_{V^\prime}$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $i_V:V\to V^\prime$ be a closed immersion such that $i^{-1}(V^\prime)=V$ and $j_{V^\prime}\circ i_V=i\circ j_V$. Write $I_i$ and $I_{i_V}$ for their kernel ideal sheaves, regarded as modules by the kernel construction [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then there exists an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{V^\prime}$-modules $j_{V^\prime}^{*}I_i\cong I_{i_V}$, where $j_{V^\prime}^{*}$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. No universal thickening or square-zero assumption is needed.

proof.text: Fix W open in V prime. Its image in the ambient scheme has inverse image under i contained in V by hpre. The section map of the source open inclusion on that inverse image is consequently an isomorphism. The commuting square, Scheme.Hom.comp_app, and the open appIso identify the zero equations for iV on W and for i on the ambient image of W. This explicitly transports kernels without assuming W affine.

source.place: Lemma 00A0 (lemma-j-pullback), including modules; Morphisms, Section 01R1 preceding Definition 01R2; More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening), open base change

proof.text: Restrict the original ideal module inclusion and compose with restrictUnitIso to obtain alpha into the restricted structure module. The kernel zero equivalence from the preceding step makes alpha factor through the restricted kernel ideal module by kernel.lift. Its component is injective because the original ideal inclusion and open section isomorphism are injective. Given a target ideal section, apply the inverse open section isomorphism to its image in the structure module; the zero equivalence puts this section in the range of the original ideal inclusion. Lift it, and use injectivity of the target ideal inclusion to show its image is the prescribed section. Thus every component is bijective and the module map is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Tensor pullback and open restriction are left adjoints of the same pushforward. Their unique comparison isomorphism, composed with the just-constructed ideal module isomorphism, gives the displayed result.

theorem nonempty_tensorPullback_open_kernel
    {Z Z' : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Z') [IsClosedImmersion i]
    {V : Z.Opens} {V' : Z'.Opens} (iV : V.toScheme ⟶ V'.toScheme)
    [IsClosedImmersion iV] (hpre : i ⁻¹ᵁ V' = V)
    (hcomm : iV ≫ V'.ι = V.ι ≫ i) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback V'.ι).obj i.ker.toModules ≅
      iV.ker.toModules)
